HARDEN-NOTEBOOK-WRITE-GATE-AC5-BLOCKING.title: Harden notebook-write AC-5 from advisory prose to BLOCKING (exit 1 -> force recompose) + commit headless-path hook backstop into repo
HARDEN-NOTEBOOK-WRITE-GATE-AC5-BLOCKING.desc: ROOT CAUSE (router pass #11, raw-verified 2026-06-15): notebook-write SKILL layer-1 gate is advisory PROSE not a hard bash gate. AC-5 (SKILL line 76) is explicitly 'a verification gate, NOT a remediation loop' — it only echoes a warning, never exit 1/blocks. This CONTRADICTS the governance founding principle (project_context_bloat_governance line 13: 'Hard bash gate, not prose — haiku skips prose'). Evidence: ops.md re-breached to 237L (working-tree; HEAD 151L) AFTER its own agent-father retrofit 1c8a5ea7; the 237L write minted NO context-bloat signal (layer-2 PostToolUse hook is record-only exit 0 AND lives in gitignored .claude/settings.local.json so headless/cron/cloud spawns don't carry it). Layer-3 janitor is the ONLY hard remediation and it's reactive — board is littered with recurring CLEAN-NB-TRIM-* / FU-NB-PRUNE-* tasks (CLEAN-NB-TRIM-BATCH = 5 notebooks 297/223/223/218/228L; CLEAN-CONTEXT-BLOAT-NOTEBOOKS-20260614; CLEAN-NB-TRIM-PDFX-2; FU-NB-PRUNE-DEV-VPS), proving the reactive churn. SCOPE (the cheap correct slice — NOT a full architecture sprint): (1) Convert AC-5 to BLOCKING for the in-session/compliant-tooling path: after the settled write, if wc -l > cap then exit 1 and force the agent to recompose+re-write (a hard gate can only FAIL the write, NOT auto-pick which sections to drop — semantic prune needs agent judgment, that is the accepted tradeoff). (2) Close the headless/cron gap: commit the PostToolUse backstop hook wiring into a REPO-TRACKED settings file (.claude/settings.json, NOT .local) so cron/headless/cloud spawns carry it — OR add a documented dumb-tail-truncate fallback in the hook for non-compliant writes as a last-resort self-heal (architect decides truncate-vs-fail-vs-signal-only). DESIGN TRADEOFF to resolve in brief: dumb tail-cut loses the newest section (usually the current cycle's content) — may be unacceptable; a fail-the-write gate can't run in a fire-and-forget headless write that has no agent loop to recompose. Architect weighs blocking-in-session + signal-only-headless vs truncate-headless.

Add a unit test: idle-queue-0-running + push-age>360min -> verdict=IDLE/INFO (not CRASH); down-service OR (queue>0 AND age>SLA) -> CRASH.

FIX-AUDITOR-C11-PDFX-STATUS-PREDICATE.title: system-auditor C-11 (pdf_documents) check predicate broken: queries status=done (never exists) + ISO-8601 vs datetime() strcompare bypass -> ALWAYS false-fails
FIX-AUDITOR-C11-PDFX-STATUS-PREDICATE.description: C-11 (docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/main.md L478 spec table + bun:sqlite probe) is: count(*) FROM pdf_documents WHERE status='done' AND extracted_at > datetime('now','-48 hours'). RAW live probe (pdf_extractor.db, 2026-06-25T00:37Z, 42233 rows): DISTINCT status = failed(40758)/processing(1376)/success(99) -- there is NO 'done' status, so the predicate ALWAYS returns 0 and C-11 false-fails on every scan. TWO bugs: (1) status literal 'done' must be 'success' (the real terminal-OK status); (2) extracted_at on success rows is ISO-8601 with T separator (e.g. 2026-06-15T22:13:09.472421) while datetime('now','-48 hours') returns space-separated, so the string compare bypasses (feedback_sqlite_iso8601_datetime_strcompare_bypass) and even after fixing the status literal the 48h window mis-evaluates. failed/processing rows have NULL extracted_at.
FIX-AUDITOR-C11-PDFX-STATUS-PREDICATE.fix_spec: Correct C-11 in BOTH the L478 spec table row AND any bun:sqlite probe block: (a) status='done' -> status='success' (verified the ONLY terminal-OK value; failed/processing are the other two). (b) Replace the ISO-8601-vs-datetime() string compare with an epoch-seconds compare so the 48h window evaluates correctly against the T-format column, e.g. WHERE status='success' AND strftime('%s',replace(extracted_at,'T',' ')) > strftime('%s','now','-48 hours'). GENERIC: no date literals. (c) C-11 is gated > 0 in the earnings window; an out-of-season 0 (Q2 filings land Jul-Aug) should be INFO not HIGH -- apply the same off-market/earnings-season-awareness pattern already prescribed for C-06 (FIX-AUDITOR-C06-OFFMARKET-RECALIBRATE).

FIX-FB-GATE-CHECKC-NEGATION-LEXICON.title: fb-gate Check-C: negation-blind to Vietnamese 'chưa' false-blocks orderly-pullback posts + \d->[0-9] BSD-grep portability
FIX-FB-GATE-CHECKC-NEGATION-LEXICON.lesson: L4 (2026-06-25 -0,80% orderly post FALSE-BLOCKED twice: 'chưa hoảng loạn'/'chưa phải bán tháo' counted AFFIRMATIVE — 'chưa' absent from Check-C negation-strip set)
FIX-FB-GATE-CHECKC-NEGATION-LEXICON.desc: Check-C builds SELLOFF_AFFIRM_LINES by removing lines that match the negation set {không phải|không có|không bán|chứ không|mà không} (line ~342). 'chưa' (not yet/not) is NOT in that set, so an explicitly-negated panic statement ('lực bán chưa hoảng loạn', 'chưa phải bán tháo') survives the strip, is counted as an AFFIRMATIVE selloff claim, and on a mild day (|VN-Index|<2%, ~0 floor) FALSE-BLOCKS a correct non-panic post. FIX (1): add 'chưa' and common variants ('chưa phải','chưa từng') to the negation-stripping lexicon. FIX (2): replace `\d` with `[0-9]` in the floor-stock regex `chỉ \d mã sàn` (line ~361) — BSD grep -E on macOS treats `\d` literally; `[0-9]` is GNU/BSD portable.
FIX-FB-GATE-CHECKC-NEGATION-LEXICON.generic_mandate: Broaden the negation lexicon generically (any 'chưa'-prefixed negation of panic language), not a one-off literal; the [0-9] portability fix applies to EVERY `\d` in the gate's grep -E patterns — audit the whole script for stray `\d` while here.

FIX-AUDITOR-SBVFX-SLA-POSTMARKET-TOLERAN.root_cause: getSlaThreshold() (freshnessSlaChecker.ts L646-652) applies the tight defaultThresholdMinutes (30) for the WHOLE VN business day whenever isVnSbvBusinessDay(now)==true. But SBV publishes FX once/day; its publish window ends 10:00 UTC (lastExpectedSbvWindowEnd L530). After 10:00Z no new sbv_fx arrives until the next business-day window, yet the 30-min tight SLA stays active all day -> age sawtooths against the ~30-min fetcher poll cadence and breaches HIGH at the top of every cycle (Fri 10:33Z age 37/30). The DONE FIX-SLA-EXEMPT-NEWS-SBVFX relaxes ONLY on non-business days (weekend/holiday); the post-publish-window-on-a-business-day window AND the SLA==poll-cadence sawtooth are uncovered. Same structural pattern hits news (tight 30-min SLA for the whole 00:00-14:59Z window vs ~30-min poll -> news sawtoothed OK->32/30 in the same tick). Same over-fire CLASS as B-11 (market-hours-blind) and C-06 (off-market).
FIX-AUDITOR-SBVFX-SLA-POSTMARKET-TOLERAN.fix_spec: 1) Post-window relaxation on business days: in the SBV branch, once now is PAST lastExpectedSbvWindowEnd for today, switch to (minutesSinceLastSbvWindowEnd + grace) instead of the tight 30-min -> the tight SLA applies DURING the expected publish window only, not all day. Mirror for news post-14:59Z. 2) Tolerance band so SLA never equals poll cadence: breach HIGH only when age > MAX(threshold*1.5, threshold + pollCadence); a 30-min SLA on a 30-min poller must not fire on a single-cycle slip. Apply uniformly to news + sbv_fx.

The 7-task HSC sprint delivered -79% (2.46MB -> 537KB) but the brief's aspirational <150KB end-state needs work NOT in the HSC decomposition. Residual hot weight: task_board.active_sprints 220KB (18 live sprints) + decision_journal 23.5KB + sprint_goal 21KB. (2) decision_journal ring-buffer (keep last N, evict remainder to cold). (3) sprint_goal prune stale entries. AC: hot orch-state.json <150KB; every genuinely-live sprint retained; jq sentinel (.head and .task_board and .signal_queue and ._meta) passes; orch-cold-evict idempotent. RECORD-ONLY — PO opened this stub at sign-off; do NOT execute now.
FU-ORCH-HOT-SUB150-SPRINT-LIFECYCLE.root_cause: active_sprints has no terminal-sprint eviction path. HSC-1 evicts terminal done/done_verified/signal rows but a SPRINT object stays in active_sprints until manually closed, so 18 sprints (incl 1 null-status) accrete 220KB in-file. decision_journal + sprint_goal grow unbounded.

FIX-PDF-EXTRACTOR-TEST-SYS-MODULES-LEAK.status_note: AC: rewrite apps/pdf-extractor/__tests__/unit/test_low_text_density_ocr_rasterize.py lines 91,102,110,123-124 so sys.modules['pdfplumber'|'fitz'|'paddleocr'|'PIL'|'PIL.Image'] stubs are either (a) applied via monkeypatch.setattr (pytest auto-restores after each test) or (b) wrapped in a fixture with explicit teardown restoring the original sys.modules entries, or (c) use this file's own already-correct _ensure_stub() conditional-check pattern (only stub if real package absent) uniformly instead of raw unconditional assignment. Evidence: PDF-TEST-01-FIX QA audit 2026-07-07 — full non-slow suite (container) 1079 passed/7 failed; all 7 traced + reproduced to this file polluting global sys.modules and leaking into test_ocr_backends.py::TestToPilAndFailLoud::test_d_tesseract_backend_pil_image_passthrough (AttributeError: PIL.Image has no attribute new), test_ocr_unit_tesseract_retry.py AC1/AC2 (same PIL.Image.new error), and test_page_rasterizer.py x4 (fake fitz stub hardcoded page_count=4 leaks into real-fitz rasterizer tests, asserts 4!=2). Repro commands: docker exec vn-market-intelligence-mcp-pdf-extractor-1 python3 -m pytest __tests__/unit/test_low_text_density_ocr_rasterize.py __tests__/test_ocr_backends.py -q (1 failed/46 passed); same file + __tests__/unit/test_page_rasterizer.py -q (4 failed/28 passed). Each file passes 100% alone. DoD: full apps/pdf-extractor/__tests__ suite (excl @pytest.mark.slow) green in one docker-exec pytest run, order-independent (verify by running the offending file both before and after the previously-broken files).
